command:
npx --yes --package @benchrouter/cli benchrouter init \
  --setup-key br_setup_x \
  --repo example/app \
  --route-id app/<route-slug> \
  --name "<Route Name>" \
  --incumbent-model <provider/model> \
  --provider-id <direct-provider> \
  --provider-ref <provider-native-model-id> \
  --base-url-env <LLM_BASE_URL_ENV> \
  --api-family <openai_chat_completions|anthropic_messages|openai_responses> \
  --code-ref <call-site-file> \
  --eval-pack <route-eval-pack.json>

guides..benchrouter/README.md:
- For a new route, run npx --yes --package @benchrouter/cli benchrouter init. For an existing route, run npx --yes --package @benchrouter/cli benchrouter upgrade. Upgrade preserves benchrouter.yml byte-for-byte and never replaces cases, scorers, calibration fixtures, setup guides, or app files.
- npx --yes --package @benchrouter/cli benchrouter doctor --phase evaluation --repo example/app
guides..benchrouter/SETUP_README.md:
npx --yes --package @benchrouter/cli benchrouter doctor --phase evaluation --repo example/app
Run `npx --yes --package @benchrouter/cli benchrouter doctor --phase activation --route-id <selected-route-id> --repo example/app`. This validates the selected route's local wiring; it makes no runtime request by default.
